# Claude Code

- **Paths:** `<setup>` is the setup checkout (CHECKOUT in the skills and commands). Find the Orc-istration checkout: the "Setup checkout (this machine)" line in the rulebook's tool notes, else `setupCheckout` in `config.json` (under `ORC_DATA_DIR` when set, else under `~/.orc/`), else ask the user. Call it CHECKOUT and confirm `CHECKOUT/tools/orc.mjs` exists there; if it does not, stop and say so. Full reference: `<setup>/orchestration/README.md`. Agent definitions: `~/.claude/agents/*.md`. Local data lives in `~/.orc/` (`ORC_DATA_DIR` when set), not in the checkout or `~/.claude`: cost log `~/.orc/log/<date>-<project>-<slug>.md` using `<setup>/orchestration/log/TEMPLATE.md`, anomaly log `~/.orc/log/anomalies.md`, and the board repo wherever `board.repo` in `~/.orc/config.json` points (suggested: `~/.orc/board`; protocol in `<board repo>/README.md`).
- **Dispatch:** always name `subagent_type`. If you don't, the agent inherits the orchestrator model, unless `settings.json` sets a subagent model: a bare Agent call, or any agent definition with no model, runs on Opus 5.5 at high effort through `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT` in `settings.json`; agents marked `model: inherit` still follow the session, and built-in Explore and Plan keep their own model. Pass `model:` only to override the roster for one dispatch (a Mid-tier override is `model: "sonnet"`). The orchestrator runs on Fable 5.2 at medium effort today.
- **Tiers:** Low = haiku, Mid = sonnet (high effort), High = opus (high effort), from `models.json`; `node tools/orc.mjs sync --apply` installs them into `~/.claude/agents/*.md`.
- **Resume and stop:** resume a builder with SendMessage; stop a drifting agent with TaskStop. For the orc CLI, tests, scratch files and worktrees, the `orc-permissions` skill adds standing allow rules (after asking the user), so fewer agents stall on a prompt. Parallel builders get `isolation: "worktree"`; it failed once on a Windows checkout, so if it errors, make the worktree with `git worktree add` and pass its path.
- **Ask:** a several-picks question to the user (such as the durable-rules question in the dotnet-azure-devops profile) is one multiSelect `AskUserQuestion`.
- **Automation:** Ultracode and Workflow are the multi-agent automation features that stay off unless asked.
- **Board, artifact backend:** `install` adds this machine's Board line below from `~/.orc/config.json` (or `--board`). Only Claude Code writes the artifact backend, with ArtifactData (load with ToolSearch `select:ArtifactData`; if absent, `select:mcp__claude-artifacts__db_get,mcp__claude-artifacts__db_write` with the UUID slug). Its `BOARD:` line adds `slug <uuid>` after the address. A headless `claude -p` run cannot approve board writes.
- **Hooks:** `tools/board-reminder.ps1` reminds the orchestrator to update the session when an agent finishes: it leaves a marker when a builder, refuter or debugger finishes and reminds the orchestrator to update the session on its next dispatch, board write or prompt. SubagentStop output goes to the finishing agent and keeps it running, so reaching the orchestrator takes a marker relayed by PostToolUse or UserPromptSubmit. `tools/guard.ps1` (PreToolUse on Bash and PowerShell) denies a commit or push to `main`, `develop` or `master`, `git stash` in a linked worktree and `git commit|push|merge|rebase|reset|clean|stash|rm|mv|checkout|switch|restore|pull|cherry-pick|revert|am` from read-only roles, and asks before a force-push or `git add -A`. The worklog and peon hooks are Claude Code extras (`adapters/claude-code/settings.example.json`, scripts under `extras/`).
- **Skills and commands:** `install` and `sync` generate them with the agents from `core/procedures.mjs`, as thin wrappers that find the checkout and follow its tool-neutral file. The `board`, `brief`, `wrap-up`, `sprint` and `repo-standards` skills (`~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, each also `/<name>`) run `orchestration/board.md`, `brief.md`, `wrap-up.md`, `sprint.md` and `standards.md`; the `/start`, `/grill`, `/draft-pr`, `/peer-review`, `/create` and `/fix-ci` commands (`~/.claude/commands/<name>.md`) run `workflows/<name>.md`; `/pre-pr-review`, `/review-verdict` and `/calibration-report` run `review/PROCEDURE.md` and `review/calibration.md`.
- **Skills:** checked-in repo skills inherit the session model. Never pin a model in them.
- **Pull request footer:** `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) and built with [Orc-istration](https://github.com/Co0pDawg/Orc-istration) 🧌`. Commit messages keep only their Co-Authored-By line.
- **Cost log:** the orchestrator's context size comes from the status line or `/context`.
- **Timed sessions (sprint mode):** pre-approve the stack's read-only and build commands in `permissions.allow` of the user-level `~/.claude/settings.json`; `/fewer-permission-prompts` helps only in an existing project with past sessions, and only for read-only calls. `/fast` speeds up the orchestrator's own output.
- **Mockups:** publish a UI mockup for approval as a private artifact.
- **Metrics:** `metrics capture` finds the current session through `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, so the review procedure passes no `--session`.

What Claude Code cannot do (generated from the adapter's gaps):
- A role with every capability gets no `tools:` line, so it keeps MCP tools such as ArtifactData; only those roles can write the artifact board.
